negative_findings.description: No functioning, publicly disclosing Serbian-system bank operating inside Kosovo was found. Legacy entities surfaced in sr search (Jugobanka/Jugbanka Kosovska Mitrovica, Kosovska Banka) appear only in directory listings and encyclopaedic entries, not as live disclosure publishers.
negative_findings.result_summary: Directory aggregators (imenik.rs, planplus.rs) and Wikipedia returned entries; no corporate site with financial statements or press releases was located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means the 'parallel banking system' side of the cell has no first-party issuer disclosure at all — everything must be reconstructed from NBS, Poštanska štedionica, government offices and local media, which raises the evidential burden on those sources.

negative_findings.description: No Serbian-language banking-industry association or aggregator specific to Kosovo was found. Searches for a Kosovo bankers' association in sr returned only CBK material.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries returned bqk-kos.org pages exclusively; no association portal in sr surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: An industry association would normally be the cheapest pointer to member banks, fee schedules and sector statistics. Its absence in sr means the Albanian-language association (if any) must be covered by the sq cell and cross-linked.

negative_findings.description: Several sr query terms are structurally noisy and must be constrained. 'Mitrovica' collides heavily with Sremska Mitrovica (Serbia proper); 'Kosovska Banka' is largely a historical/encyclopaedic entity; 'platni promet' alone returns generic Serbian domestic-payments content.
negative_findings.result_summary: The query 'Kosovska Mitrovica sever bankarske usluge platne kartice dinar' returned at least one irrelevant Sremska Mitrovica bank-directory result.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Untuned sr queries will pollute the collection pipeline with Serbia-proper banking content; queries must pin 'Kosovska Mitrovica'/'sever Kosova'/'KiM' and exclude 'Sremska'.

negative_findings.description: This cell is scoped to sr and regional/en coverage; no Albanian-language (sq) searching was performed here beyond incidental sq artefacts (EBRD PSD in Albanian, 'raportet vjetore').
negative_findings.result_summary: sq coverage intentionally deferred to the sq-scoped cells.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents double-counting but means the run must confirm that another cell actually covers sq issuer/regulator disclosure, or the primary-market view is incomplete.

negative_findings.description: Two candidate hosts were not fetched in this pass and their access status is a hypothesis, not a verdict: kim.gov.rs (Kancelarija za KiM) and posted.co.rs (observed only over http on a legacy path).
negative_findings.result_summary: Both were surfaced via search-result context rather than a direct successful fetch of the section pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic liveness pass must resolve current canonical hosts before these are scheduled for collection; a legacy http path is a redirect/relocation risk, not evidence of a dead site.

coverage_gaps.description: No source found that quantifies banking access in Serb-majority municipalities (branch counts, ATM density, card penetration, account ownership) after the 2024 dinar measures and branch closures.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test whether CBK's Serbian-language financial stability reports or periodic statistics break down by municipality; if not, treat municipality-level access as a structural data gap and consider FOI-style requests to CBK and NBS.

coverage_gaps.description: No sr-language POINTER source (link directory, media monitor, curated dossier) covering Kosovo banking/payments was identified; all sr finds are direct institutional or indirect news sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe Belgrade economic think-tanks and media-monitoring services (e.g. Fiskalni savet, CEVES, Ekapija/Nova ekonomija tag pages) for standing Kosovo-finance dossiers that could act as pointers.

coverage_gaps.description: Remittances/diaspora transfers into Kosovo — a dominant payment flow — are covered only obliquely; no dedicated corridor-pricing source (e.g. Remittance Prices Worldwide corridor data for Kosovo) was confirmed in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and register the World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide corridor dataset and CBK remittance statistics as explicit candidates in a follow-up pass.

coverage_gaps.description: Payment-scheme and fintech actors (card schemes, PSPs, money-transfer operators licensed by CBK) were not reached in this cell; coverage stopped at banks and regulators.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest the CBK register of licensed financial institutions (available in sr) to enumerate non-bank payment institutions and MTOs, then scout each as a disclosure source.

coverage_gaps.description: Cyrillic-script sr sources are under-sampled: only the NBS media Q&A page surfaced in Cyrillic, and searches were run predominantly in Latin script.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run the seed queries transliterated into Cyrillic (банкарски сектор, платни промет, динар, Косовска Митровица) — Serbian institutional sites frequently serve script-specific content and search indexes treat the scripts separately.

brief: Serbian-language coverage of Kosovo banking splits cleanly into three tiers: authoritative bilingual regulator output (the CBK's full ?lang=sr mirror of annual reports, financial stability reports and payment regulations is the single highest-value find, and it is routinely overlooked because analysts search only the Albanian site), Belgrade institutional counter-disclosure (NBS statements, Kancelarija za KiM, Banka Poštanska štedionica as the operator of the blocked budget-payout channel), and a dense but partisan local news layer in north Kosovo and the enclaves (KoSSev, Radio Kontakt Plus, Radio KIM, Kosovo Online) that heavily cross-republishes and needs deduplication and corroboration. The parallel-system story has no first-party issuer disclosure at all — legacy Serbian-system banks in Kosovo publish nothing — so branch closures, card and ATM access, and the pension-payout workaround at administrative crossings must be reconstructed from bank customer notices, state-fund figures reported in the Serbian press, and RFE/RL's cross-checking. Regional and English-language material (World Bank payments modernization and SEPA work, BIS-archived CBK speeches, Raiffeisen Research's CEE banking report, EBRD project disclosures which also exist in Serbian translation) supplies the comparative and cross-border-cost frame that neither national source set provides. The main residual risks are municipality-level access data, non-bank payment institutions and remittance corridor pricing, plus an under-sampled Cyrillic script layer.
